sentences.text: Mr. Abdullah P., learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the accused/petitioners are the employees under Assam Power Distribution Company Ltd. (in short 'APDCL') who are presently posted at Chapor Electrical Sub-Division and they have performed their duty by disconnecting the electricity connection in regard to default of payment made by the complainant.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 15 July, 2024.json

sentences.text:
It is contended by the petitioners that the complainant had defaulted to make payment of an amount of Rs. 32,136/-
(Rupees Thirty-two thousand one hundred thirty-six) only to APDCL, Chapor Electrical Sub-Division against the consumption of energy since last September' 2023 to February' 2024.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 15 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: As per last bill dated 19.02.2024, the complainant has consumed total 3145 Units of electricity against which payable amount is of Rs.22,886/- (Twenty-two thousand eight hundred eighty-six) only in addition to an arrear amount of Rs. 2879/- (Rupees Two thousand seventy-nine) only.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 15 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: Thus, the outstanding payable amount becomes Rs.32,136/- (Rupees Thirty-two thousand one Page No.# 4/4 hundred thirty-six) only as on 19 th February, 2024.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 15 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: Thus, only on the ground of disconnection of the electricity connection, the complainant lodged the FIR against the present petitioners with some false and concocted allegation.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 15 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: More so, he submits that the petitioners are employed at the time of commission of offence with the affairs of the State Government, so it is the mandate of law that prosecution sanction be needed prior to summoning the present petitioners, but, no prosecution sanction has been obtained in the present case prior to taking cognizance of offence vide order dated 09.04.2024 and as such the impugned order dated 09.04.2024 is liable to be set aside and quashed.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 15 July, 2024.json

sentences.text:
He further submitted that the power company has the statutory right to disconnect the electrical connection of a consumer on a valid reason of being defaulter of payment of energy charges and hence, in the instant case also the complainant had filed the Complaint Case No.139/2024 which itself is not maintainable and thus,
he prays for stay of the aforesaid proceedings, till disposal of the instant criminal petition.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 15 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: Considering the submissions of learned counsels of both sides, further proceedings of the impugned Complaint Case No.139/2024 registered under Sections 120(B)/420/294/506 of IPC pending before the Court of learned Sub- Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Bilasipara and the impugned cognizance Order dated 09.04.2024, stands stayed, till disposal of the instant criminal petition.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 15 July, 2024.json

sentences.text: List the matter after 3 (three) weeks.

sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text: 1. Heard Mr. N.K. Kalita, the learned counsel for the petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text: Also heard Mr. K.K. Das, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the State of Assam.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text:
2. This application under Section 528 of the BNSS has been filed by the petitioner, namely, Shri Pabitra Saikia, who is praying for quashing the entire criminal proceeding of PRC Case No.
1861/2020, arising out of Dispur P.S. Case No. 2212/2019.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text:
3. The facts relevant for consideration of the instant criminal petition, in brief, are that on 25.07.2019, one Toulchi Sahu had lodged an FIR before the Officer-In-Charge of Dispur Police Station, inter alia, alleging that the present petitioner had stolen the cheque leafs, from his house and thereafter, manipulating the said cheque used it for drawing a total amount of Rs. 2,20,000/-
(Rupees Two Lakhs Twenty Thousand only) from the account of the informant.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text: 4. On receipt of the said FIR, Dispur P.S. Case No. 2212/2019 was registered under Section 379/420 IPC and investigation was initiated.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text: After completion of the investigation, charge sheet was laid on 30.11.2020.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text: 5. The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner appeared before the Trial Court and faced the trial and on 30.03.2023, charges under Section 379/420 of the Indian Penal Code Page No.# 3/4 were framed against him.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text: He submits that though the matter involved in the case is of civil nature, however, he faced the trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text: 6. The learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that on 21.12.2021, the PW-1 was examined and his further examination was kept reserved and till that day for last 3 years 08 months, his trial is going on, without any progress and no further prosecution witness has been examined till date.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text:
7. Mr. K.K. Das, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor, on the other hand submits that in this case, charges are already framed and trial is going on and therefore, it is not a fit case for invoking the inherent jurisdiction for quashing the entire proceeding under Section 528 of the BNSS, 2023.
8.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for both the sides.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text: It appears that though the charges were framed in the year 2021, the petitioner has approached this Court for quashing the proceeding after a long time of about 04 years.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Further, considering the fact that the charges are already been framed and trial is going on, this Court is of the considered opinion that this is not a fit case for quashing the entire criminal proceeding of PRC Case No. 1861/2020.
9.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text: However, it is also a matter of concern that since 21.12.2021, the case is pending at the stage of examination of prosecution witnesses and only one witness has been examined, that too, in part.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text:
10. Under such circumstances, while disposing of this criminal petition, this Court is constrained to direct the Trial Court to make all Page No.# 4/4 endeavours to dispose of the PRC Case No.
1861/2020, as expeditiously as possible.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text: 11. With the above observations, this criminal petition is disposed of.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 10 February, 2025.json

sentences.text:
2. This is an application filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C., 1973, assailing the legality and validity of the order dated 10.08.2023, passed by the Hon'ble Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Lakhimpur, North Lakhimpur in petition no. 1441/2023, filed under Section 239 of the Cr.P.C., in P.R. Case No. 1215/2019 of Bihpuria P.S. Case NO. 261/2012 (G.R. Case No. 1502/2012),
registered under Sections 420/468/34 of the IPC.

entities.text: Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Lakhimpur, North Lakhimpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025.json

sentences.text:
3. The petitioners' case is that though the petitioners had filed a discharge petition being petition no.
1441/2023, under Section 239 of the Cr.P.C., praying for discharging them from the offences under Sections 420/468/34 of the IPC, the same was rejected by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, North-Lakhimpur, without any valid reasons.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: 4. It is the case of the petitioners that though the petitioners were actually not involved in the aforesaid offences as alleged in the FIR and though there were no Page No.# 3/4 specific allegations against the petitioners, the petitioners were charge-sheeted.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: 5. The learned counsel appearing for the accused petitioners submits that from the statements recorded before the police, it is found that none of the victims had actually alleged any kind of cheating against the accused petitioners rather, there are certain allegations against one Rubul Gogoi, who is the husband of the accused petitioner no. 1, Bandana Gogoi.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: The learned counsel further submits that though there are certain allegations against the aforesaid accused person Rubul Gogoi, he has already been discharged by the police as no charge-sheet was filed against him.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid, the learned counsel submits that since the main accused has not been charge- sheeted by the police, the order passed by the learned JMFC, North-Lakhimpur is apparently and palpably wrong whereby the petitioners were not discharged.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Therefore, he submits that the Page No.# 1/4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192226420/
2 proceedings before the learned JMFC, Lakhimpur may be stayed till the disposal of the petition.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: 6. Mr. P. Borthakur, learned Addl. P.P. appearing for the State submits that there is no illegality in the order passed by the learned JMFC, North-Lakhimpur.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, no interim order, as prayed for, should be granted.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: 7. This Court has gone through the materials brought before this Court as well as perused the Trial Court records that has been placed before this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: 8. On perusal of the TCR as well as on considering the submissions of the counsel appearing for their respective parties, this Court is of the considered view that, at this stage, further proceedings of the P.R. Case No. 1215/2019, pending before the Court of JMFC, North-Lakhimpur, should be stayed till the disposal of the instant criminal petition.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025.json

sentences.text: 9. In view of the aforesaid findings, the proceedings of P.R. Case No. 1215/2019, pending before the Court of JMFC, North-Lakhimpur is stayed.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-4 vs The State Of Assam And Anr on 4 December, 2025.json

sentences.text:
10. Let the matter be listed again in the 2nd week of January, 2026.

opennyai_summary.15_July_2024__arguments:
It is contended by the petitioners that the complainant had defaulted to make payment of an amount of Rs. 32,136/-
(Rupees Thirty-two thousand one hundred thirty-six) only to APDCL, Chapor Electrical Sub-Division against the consumption of energy since last September' 2023 to February' 2024.
More so, he submits that the petitioners are employed at the time of commission of offence with the affairs of the State Government, so it is the mandate of law that prosecution sanction be needed prior to summoning the present petitioners, but, no prosecution sanction has been obtained in the present case prior to taking cognizance of offence vide order dated 09.04.2024 and as such the impugned order dated 09.04.2024 is liable to be set aside and quashed.
He further submitted that the power company has the statutory right to disconnect the electrical connection of a consumer on a valid reason of being defaulter of payment of energy charges and hence, in the instant case also the complainant had filed the Complaint Case No.139/2024 which itself is not maintainable and thus,
he prays for stay of the aforesaid proceedings, till disposal of the instant criminal petition.
opennyai_summary.15_July_2024__facts: Thus, only on the ground of disconnection of the electricity connection, the complainant lodged the FIR against the present petitioners with some false and concocted allegation.
